Class LeaderboardRepository

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.it.network.server.persistence.LeaderboardRepository
public class LeaderboardRepository extends Object
Data Access Object for the leaderboard.

Encapsulates every read/write operation against the DatabaseInitializer.TABLE_NAME table. The class is intentionally stateless apart from the configuration: each public method opens its own connection via DriverManager and closes it through try-with-resources, so the repository is safe to share across threads.

Operations:

  • saveGameResults(List, int) — persists the rows of one completed game in a single transaction and returns the timestamp actually stored;
  • getLeaderboard(int) — returns the full ranked leaderboard for games of a given size;
  • getPlayerRank(String, int, int, LocalDateTime) — computes the position of one specific result against all other games with the same number of players.

  • Method Details

    • saveGameResults

      public LocalDateTime saveGameResults(List<LeaderboardEntry> entries, int numPlayers) throws SQLException
      Persists the result of a completed game.

      All rows are inserted inside a single transaction, sharing the same game_uuid and played_at timestamp. If the first entry already carries a timestamp, that value is used for the whole game; otherwise the repository generates one. The timestamp is normalised to seconds because the table stores it in a MySQL DATETIME column without fractional seconds.

      Parameters:
      entries - one entry per participant; the rank field is ignored (ranks are recomputed by the queries)
      numPlayers - number of players that took part — used to override the per-entry value if missing
      Returns:
      the timestamp actually stored for the game, or null if entries is empty
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the database is unreachable or rejects the statements

      public List<LeaderboardEntry> getLeaderboard(int numPlayers) throws SQLException

      Parameters:
      numPlayers - number of players the games of interest had
      Returns:

    • getPlayerRank

      public int getPlayerRank(String nickname, int finalScore, int numPlayers, LocalDateTime playedAt) throws SQLException
      Computes the position (1-based) of a single result among all the games with the same number of players.

      The query counts how many rows have a strictly higher score, plus how many have the same score but were played strictly earlier; the rank of the result is one more than that count. This avoids loading the full leaderboard just to find a single position.

      Parameters:
      nickname - nickname of the player whose result we are placing
      finalScore - score the player obtained in the game of interest
      numPlayers - number of players in the game of interest
      playedAt - timestamp of the game of interest (must match the one used when saving)
      Returns:
      the 1-based rank of the result
      Throws:
      SQLException
